bio: Irish avant-garde dramatist and novelist awarded the 1969 Nobel Prize, author of Waiting for Godot, Endgame, and his landmark trilogy Molloy, Malone Dies, and The Unnamable.

name: Alexander Solzhenitsyn
bio: Russian novelist, historian, and dissident awarded the 1970 Nobel Prize, whose One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich and The Gulag Archipelago exposed the Soviet camp system.

name: Heinrich Böll
bio: One of post-war Germany's foremost writers, 1972 Nobel laureate celebrated for his humane moral conscience in Billiards at Half-Past Nine and The Lost Honour of Katharina Blum.

name: Patrick White
bio: The only Australian author to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1973), hailed for introducing a continent into world literature with visionary epics like Voss and The Eye of the Storm.

name: Elias Canetti
bio: Bulgarian-born modernist polymath awarded the 1981 Nobel Prize, author of the devastating psychological novel Auto-da-Fé and sociological study Crowds and Power.

name: Claude Simon
bio: French Nouveau Roman novelist awarded the 1985 Nobel Prize, acclaimed for intertwining personal memory, sensory perception, and war in The Flanders Road and The Georgics.

name: Naguib Mahfouz
bio: Egyptian writer and the first Arabic-language author to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1988), master of the modern novel renowned for his monumental Cairo Trilogy.

name: Camilo José Cela
bio: Spanish novelist and 1989 Nobel laureate, leading figure of the tremendismo movement in post-Civil War Spain, acclaimed for The Family of Pascual Duarte and The Hive.

name: Kenzaburō Ōe
bio: Japanese author awarded the 1994 Nobel Prize for creating an imagined world where myth and reality condense to picture human predicament in A Personal Matter and The Silent Cry.

name: Günter Grass
bio: German novelist, poet, and dramatist awarded the 1999 Nobel Prize, whose Danzig Trilogy beginning with The Tin Drum portrayed the forgotten face of history with frolicsome black fables.

name: Gao Xingjian
bio: Chinese-born French novelist and playwright awarded the 2000 Nobel Prize, acclaimed for his monumental episodic novel Soul Mountain.

name: Imre Kertész
bio: Hungarian author and Holocaust survivor awarded the 2002 Nobel Prize for writing that upholds the fragile experience of the individual against the barbaric arbitrariness of history in Fatelessness.

name: Elfriede Jelinek
bio: Austrian playwright and novelist awarded the 2004 Nobel Prize for her musical flow of voices in works like The Piano Teacher exposing the absurdity of society's clichés.

name: Doris Lessing
bio: British-Zimbabwean novelist awarded the 2007 Nobel Prize, that epicist of the female experience whose masterpiece The Golden Notebook transformed modern feminist fiction.

name: J. M. G. Le Clézio
bio: French-Mauritian author awarded the 2008 Nobel Prize, explorer of a humanity beyond and below the reigning civilization in Desert and The Interrogation.

name: Mario Vargas Llosa
bio: Peruvian-Spanish novelist and 2010 Nobel laureate, leading figure of the Latin American Boom celebrated for The Feast of the Goat, The Time of the Hero, and Aunt Julia and the Scriptwriter.

name: Mo Yan
bio: Chinese novelist awarded the 2012 Nobel Prize for hallucinatory realism merging folk tales, history, and the contemporary in Red Sorghum and Life and Death Are Wearing Me Out.

name: Patrick Modiano
bio: French novelist awarded the 2014 Nobel Prize for the art of memory with which he has evoked the most ungraspable human destinies and uncovered the life-world of the Nazi Occupation in Missing Person.

name: Peter Handke
bio: Austrian novelist, playwright, and translator awarded the 2019 Nobel Prize for an influential work that with linguistic ingenuity has explored the periphery and the specificity of human experience in The Goalie's Anxiety at the Penalty Kick.

name: Abdulrazak Gurnah
bio: Zanzibar-born British novelist awarded the 2021 Nobel Prize for his uncompromising and compassionate penetration of the effects of colonialism and the fate of the refugee in Paradise, By the Sea, and Afterlives.

name: Jon Fosse
bio: Norwegian dramatist and novelist awarded the 2023 Nobel Prize in Literature for his innovative plays and prose which give voice to the unsayable, author of the visionary seven-part epic Septology.
